sections.title: 1. Ingredients and Keywords of the Preamble

masteryZone.q: Which of the following describes the correct order of keywords in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
opts: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic
Sovereign, Secular, Socialist, Democratic, Republic
Socialist, Secular, Sovereign, Democratic, Republic
Sovereign, Socialist, Democratic, Secular, Republic
masteryZone.sol: The correct sequence is: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.

masteryZone.q: Who among the following constitutional experts called the Preamble the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'?
opts: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
K.M. Munshi
N.A. Palkhivala
Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer
masteryZone.sol: N.A. Palkhivala, an eminent jurist, referred to the Preamble as the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is based on the 'Objective Resolution' which was drafted and moved by whom?
opts: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Jawaharlal Nehru
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble is based on the 'Objective Resolution', drafted and moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946, and adopted on January 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: In which year was the Preamble amended for the first and only time?
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble has been amended only once, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, which added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.

masteryZone.q: Which keyword in the Preamble implies that India is free to conduct its internal and external affairs without any foreign interference?
opts: Sovereign
Socialist
Democratic
Republic
masteryZone.sol: Sovereignty implies that India is independent, with no authority above it, and free to manage its own domestic and foreign policies.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976? (Select all that apply)
opts: Socialist
Secular
Integrity
Fraternity
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Amendment Act added the terms: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are the key ingredients of the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: Source of authority of the Constitution
Nature of the Indian State
Objectives of the Constitution
Detailed procedure of constitutional amendment
masteryZone.sol: The four ingredients are: Source of authority (People of India), Nature of the state, Objectives, and Date of adoption. It does not contain amendment procedures.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following represent the democratic credentials of the Indian state? (Select all that apply)
opts: Universal adult franchise
Periodic elections
Rule of law
Hereditary office of the President
masteryZone.sol: Universal adult franchise, periodic elections, and rule of law are elements of democracy. The President of India is elected, not hereditary (which is monarchy).

masteryZone.q: Which terms denote the nature of the Indian State in the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: Sovereign
Socialist
Secular
Federal
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble defines India as Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic. The word 'Federal' is not in the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: Select the features of democratic socialism as practiced in India: (Select all that apply)
opts: Mixed economy with public and private sectors
Ending poverty, ignorance, disease, and inequality of opportunity
Abolition of all private property
State control over all means of production
masteryZone.sol: Indian socialism is Democratic Socialism, which believes in a mixed economy and aims to end poverty/ignorance, unlike Communistic/State socialism which nationalizes all property.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is a source of power to the legislature and can limit legislative jurisdiction.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Preamble is neither a source of power to the legislature nor a limitation on its powers.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble was adopted by the Constituent Assembly before the rest of the Constitution was passed.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution was already passed to ensure it aligned with all provisions.

masteryZone.q: India is a democratic monarchy because it has a Parliament but also recognizes the British Crown.
masteryZone.sol: False. India is a democratic republic with an elected head of state and no allegiance to the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were part of the original Preamble adopted in 1949.
masteryZone.sol: False. They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: India practices positive secularism where the state treats all religions equally and supports them.
masteryZone.sol: True. Positive secularism means that all religions in the country have the same status and support from the state.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble represents the ultimate sovereignty of the Parliament over the people of India.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Preamble starts with 'We, the People of India...', indicating popular sovereignty (sovereignty of the people).

masteryZone.q: The United States was the first country to begin its Constitution with a Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: True. The US Constitution was indeed the first to adopt a Preamble.

masteryZone.q: The preamble is non-justiciable in the courts of law.
masteryZone.sol: True. Its provisions are not enforceable in any court of law.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is based on the ______ Resolution drafted and moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
masteryZone.sol: The Objective Resolution formed the basis of the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble has been amended only ______ time(s) so far.
masteryZone.sol: It was amended only once, by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: The state where the head of state is elected and not hereditary is called a ______.
masteryZone.sol: A Republic has an elected head of state.

masteryZone.q: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble by the ______ Constitutional Amendment Act.
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Amendment Act added 'Secular'.

masteryZone.q: The source of authority of the Indian Constitution is the ______ of India.
masteryZone.sol: The authority is derived from 'We, the People of India'.

masteryZone.q: India is a ______ Democratic Republic as per the sequence of terms in the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: The sequence starts: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.

masteryZone.q: N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the '______ Card of the Constitution'.
masteryZone.sol: He called it the Identity Card of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: The date of adoption of the Constitution mentioned in the Preamble is November 26, ______.
masteryZone.sol: The date is November 26, 1949.

masteryZone.q: Match the Preamble keywords with their core descriptions:

options.text: All religions have equal status and support

masteryZone.sol: Republic means elected head; Sovereign means independent; Secular means equality of all religions.

masteryZone.q: Match the terms with their constitutional aspects:
masteryZone.sol: Objective Resolution was moved by Nehru; 42nd CAA added three words; Palkhivala called Preamble the Identity Card.

masteryZone.q: Match the dates with their historical milestones:
masteryZone.sol: December 13, 1946: Resolution moved; January 22, 1947: Resolution adopted; November 26, 1949: Constitution adopted.

masteryZone.q: What is the decryption of 'S' in the sequence 'SDR' for Preamble keywords?
masteryZone.sol: Sovereign (or Socialist, or Secular, as the first three words start with S).

masteryZone.q: Who drafted the Objective Resolution?
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru.

masteryZone.q: Which country first began its constitution with a Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: The United States of America (USA).

masteryZone.q: Is the Preamble justiciable?
masteryZone.sol: No, it is non-justiciable.

masteryZone.q: How many times has the Preamble been amended?
masteryZone.sol: Only once, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: What is the source of authority of the Constitution as per the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: The People of India.

masteryZone.q: What date of adoption is specified in the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: November 26, 1949.

masteryZone.q: What does a mixed economy denote in Indian Socialism?
masteryZone.sol: Co-existence of both public and private sectors in the economy.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is non-justiciable.
Reason (R): Its provisions cannot be enforced in a court of law.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Non-justiciable means not enforceable in a court of law. Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): India is a Republic.
Reason (R): The President of India is elected and is not a hereditary monarch.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A republic is characterized by an elected head of state, which explains why India is a republic.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is a source of power to the Parliament.
Reason (R): The Preamble outlines the supreme authority of the citizens of India.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false because the Preamble is NOT a source of power to the legislature. Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble in 1976.
Reason (R): The 42nd Amendment Act added Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why/how Secular was added in 1976.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble was adopted before all other provisions of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The Preamble forms the introductory notes of the Constitution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false because the Preamble was adopted *after* the other provisions. Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the identity card of the Constitution.
Reason (R): It summarizes the fundamental values and ideals of the Constitution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why it is called the 'identity card' (as it summarizes core values).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Indian Socialism is Democratic Socialism.
Reason (R): It aims to end poverty, ignorance, and inequality of opportunity through mixed economy.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and democratic socialism in India is characterized by mixed economy to end poverty and inequality.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble cannot be amended under any circumstances.
Reason (R): It contains elements of the Basic Structure of the Constitution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false. The Preamble *can* be amended under Article 368, except its basic structure. Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The term 'Secular' was absent from the Preamble before the 42nd Amendment, but India was already secular under Articles 25-28.
Statement II: The Preamble was enacted before all other parts of the Constitution were passed.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because the Preamble was enacted after other parts.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble represents popular sovereignty because it derives its authority from the People of India.
Statement II: Republic implies that public offices are open to all citizens without discrimination.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Popular sovereignty is rooted in the people, and republic implies open public offices without discrimination.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble is justiciable and fully enforceable in courts.
Statement II: The Preamble is neither a source of power to legislature nor a limitation.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect because it is non-justiciable. Statement II is correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble has been amended three times since 1950.
Statement II: The 42nd Amendment added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect (amended only once). Statement II is correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble is based on the Objective Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946.
Statement II: The Objective Resolution was adopted unanimously by the Constituent Assembly in 1947.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Preamble considered key to interpret the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Because it contains the fundamental values, ideals, and philosophy on which the Constitution is built, assisting the judiciary to resolve ambiguities in other articles.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Preamble enacted after the rest of the Constitution had already been passed?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure that the Preamble was in perfect conformity and alignment with all the articles, parts, and schedules of the final Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Why is Indian Secularism called 'Positive Secularism'?
masteryZone.sol: Because rather than strictly separating religion and state (like in the West), the Indian state treats all religions equally, giving them the same respect, status, and protection.

masteryZone.q: How does the opening phrase 'We, the People of India...' establish popular sovereignty?
masteryZone.sol: It states that the Constitution is created, adopted, and given to ourselves by the citizens, demonstrating that the people are the ultimate source of all political and constitutional authority.

masteryZone.q: How did the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 alter the description of India in the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: It changed the description of India from a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' to a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic', and changed 'unity of the Nation' to 'unity and integrity of the Nation'.

masteryZone.q: How does democratic socialism differ from communistic socialism?
masteryZone.sol: Democratic socialism supports a mixed economy where both public and private sectors coexist, aiming to eliminate poverty and inequality. Communistic socialism involves complete nationalization of all property and state monopoly over all production.

masteryZone.q: Examine the sovereignty aspect if India has to cede a portion of its territory to a neighboring nation under a land boundary agreement. How is this authorized?
masteryZone.sol: Sovereignty implies that India is free to cede its territory to a foreign state. The Supreme Court in the Berubari Union Case (1960) ruled that cession of territory cannot be done under Article 3 but requires a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368.

masteryZone.q: A private business challenges a government nationalization scheme, claiming it violates the Preamble's promise of mixed-economy socialism. Analyze the validity of this challenge.
masteryZone.sol: The challenge is invalid because: 1) The Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be used to strike down a law on its own. 2) Democratic socialism in India allows the state to nationalize key sectors for public interest while maintaining a mixed economy, which is valid under Article 19(6).

masteryZone.q: A state legislature passes a law declaring a particular local language as the sole medium of instruction. Some citizens argue this violates 'Liberty of thought and expression'. Evaluate this in light of the Preamble's objectives.
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble promises Liberty of thought and expression, which is protected under Article 19 (Freedom of Speech) and Articles 29-30 (Cultural and Educational Rights). The court will balance the state's interest in promoting regional languages with the citizens' rights to receive education in their mother tongue.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of Republic and how it promotes political equality in India.
masteryZone.sol: A republic has two main dimensions: 1) The head of the state is elected, not hereditary (like a monarchy). 2) All public offices are open to every citizen without any discrimination. This eliminates any privileged class and ensures political equality for all citizens.

masteryZone.q: Explain the four core ingredients of the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble contains four main elements: 1) Source of authority (We, the People). 2) Nature of Indian State (Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic). 3) Objectives of the Constitution (Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity). 4) Date of adoption (November 26, 1949).

masteryZone.q: Provide a brief guide on the sequence of keywords in the Preamble and their significance.
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble declares India to be a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. This sequence outlines the character of the nation: independent from external control (Sovereign), seeking social and economic welfare (Socialist), treating all religions equally (Secular), governed by elected representatives (Democratic), and headed by an elected President (Republic).

sections.title: 2. Core Objectives: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity

masteryZone.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the dimensions of Justice explicitly promised in the Preamble?
opts: Social
Economic
Political
Religious
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble promises Social, Economic, and Political Justice. It does not promise religious justice.

masteryZone.q: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble were adopted from the:
opts: Russian Revolution
French Revolution
American War of Independence
Irish Constitution
masteryZone.sol: These ideals were adopted from the French Revolution of 1789.

masteryZone.q: Which article of the Constitution is most closely linked to securing 'Equality of status and of opportunity'?
opts: Article 14
Article 19
Article 21
Article 32
masteryZone.sol: Article 14 (Equality before law) along with Articles 15, 16, 17, and 18 secure civic equality of status and opportunity.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble secures Liberty of belief, faith, and worship. Which part of the Constitution makes this right justiciable?
opts: Part III (Fundamental Rights)
Part IV (Directive Principles)
Part IVA (Fundamental Duties)
Part IX (Panchayats)
masteryZone.sol: The Liberty of belief, faith, and worship is protected as a justiciable right under the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) in Part III.

masteryZone.q: The concept of 'Fraternity' in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution emphasizes:
opts: The dominance of the state
A sense of common brotherhood and dignity of the individual
Strict separation of executive and judiciary
Equal distribution of land resources
masteryZone.sol: Fraternity promotes a sense of common brotherhood and assures the dignity of the individual along with the unity and integrity of the nation.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following liberties are explicitly mentioned in the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: Liberty of Thought
Liberty of Expression
Liberty of Association
Liberty of Worship
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble mentions: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship. 'Liberty of Association' is not explicitly listed in the Preamble (though it is a Fundamental Right under Article 19).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following match the values in the Preamble with their historical origins? (Select all that apply)
opts: Justice (Social, Economic, Political) - Russian Revolution
Liberty, Equality, Fraternity - French Revolution
Republic - US Constitution
Sovereignty - British Crown
masteryZone.sol: Justice is from the Russian Revolution (1917). Liberty, Equality, Fraternity is from the French Revolution. Republic is also from France. Sovereign is not from the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: Which provisions of the Constitution promote the value of 'Fraternity'? (Select all that apply)
opts: Single Citizenship
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A)
Directive Principles (Article 38)
Emergency Provisions
masteryZone.sol: Single citizenship and Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, which makes it a duty to promote harmony and brotherhood) directly promote Fraternity.

masteryZone.q: Equality promised in the Preamble has which of the following dimensions? (Select all that apply)
opts: Civic Equality
Political Equality
Economic Equality
Social Superiority
masteryZone.sol: Equality includes civic (Articles 14-18), political (Articles 325, 326), and economic (Article 39) dimensions. It does not promote social superiority.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are examples of political equality in India? (Select all that apply)
opts: No person is declared ineligible for inclusion in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex (Article 325)
Elections to Lok Sabha and State Assemblies are based on adult suffrage (Article 326)
Equal pay for equal work (Article 39)
Abolition of untouchability (Article 17)
masteryZone.sol: Articles 325 and 326 secure political equality. Equal pay is economic equality, and abolition of untouchability is civic/social equality.

masteryZone.q: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity are completely independent and can be applied in isolation.
masteryZone.sol: False. Dr. Ambedkar emphasized they form a union of trinity; divorcing one from the other ruins the purpose of democracy.

masteryZone.q: Social Justice implies that there is a complete absence of any social distinctions based on caste, color, race, religion, or sex.
masteryZone.sol: True. Social justice ensures equal treatment of all citizens without any social distinctions.

masteryZone.q: Economic Justice means that discrimination between people based on economic factors like wealth and income is permitted.
masteryZone.sol: False. Economic justice means non-discrimination on the basis of economic factors.

masteryZone.q: Liberty of the individual as promised in the Preamble means absolute freedom without any restrictions.
masteryZone.sol: False. Liberty is qualified and must be exercised in accordance with constitutional limitations.

masteryZone.q: The word 'Integrity' in the Preamble is associated with the objective of Fraternity.
masteryZone.sol: True. Fraternity must assure both the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.

masteryZone.q: The concept of Justice in the Preamble is secured primarily through the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) and Fundamental Rights.
masteryZone.sol: True. Both Part III and Part IV contain provisions to secure social, economic, and political justice.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble promises equality of status but not equality of opportunity.
masteryZone.sol: False. It guarantees equality of both 'status and of opportunity'.

masteryZone.q: Fraternity is promoted in India by the system of double citizenship (state and national).
masteryZone.sol: False. It is promoted by single citizenship, which fosters a sense of common brotherhood.

masteryZone.q: The French Revolution of 1789 gave birth to the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and ______.
masteryZone.sol: The triad is Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.

masteryZone.q: Justice in the Preamble includes Social, Economic, and ______ dimensions.
masteryZone.sol: The three dimensions are Social, Economic, and Political.

masteryZone.q: The objective of ______ aims to eliminate barriers based on caste, class, and creed.
masteryZone.sol: Social justice seeks to remove distinctions based on caste, creed, or class.

masteryZone.q: The term ______ in the Preamble guarantees the absence of restraint on individual activities.
masteryZone.sol: Liberty means the absence of restraints on individual actions.

masteryZone.q: Equality of status and opportunity is detailed in Articles ______ to 18.
masteryZone.sol: Articles 14 to 18 deal with the Right to Equality.

masteryZone.q: The Russian Revolution of ______ inspired the ideals of justice in the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: It took place in 1917.

masteryZone.q: The word 'Integrity' was added to Fraternity in the Preamble by the ______ Constitutional Amendment.
masteryZone.sol: It was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

masteryZone.q: Universal adult suffrage is a tool to secure ______ equality in India.
masteryZone.sol: It secures political equality.

masteryZone.q: Match the objectives with their constitutional targets:

options.text: One person, one vote, one value (Article 326)

masteryZone.sol: Social justice means no discrimination; Liberty of worship is religious freedom; Political equality is adult suffrage.

masteryZone.q: Match the objectives with their historical inspirations:
masteryZone.sol: Justice is from the Russian Revolution; Liberty/Equality/Fraternity is French Revolution; Republic is French Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Match the equality dimensions with their articles:
masteryZone.sol: Civic: Art. 14-18; Political: Art. 325-326; Economic: Art. 39.

masteryZone.q: What revolution inspired the three types of justice in the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: The Russian Revolution (1917).

masteryZone.q: What is the trinity of values that Dr. Ambedkar spoke of?
masteryZone.sol: Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.

masteryZone.q: Which article of DPSP is directly aimed at securing a social order for justice?
masteryZone.sol: Article 38.

masteryZone.q: Does the Preamble guarantee liberty of action?
masteryZone.sol: No, it guarantees liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship.

masteryZone.q: Name the amendment that added 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: What are the two components fraternity must assure?
masteryZone.sol: Dignity of the individual and unity & integrity of the nation.

masteryZone.q: Which article secures equality of opportunity in public employment?
masteryZone.sol: Article 16.

masteryZone.q: Is the liberty promised in the Preamble absolute or qualified?
masteryZone.sol: It is qualified (subject to reasonable restrictions).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble promises political equality to all citizens.
Reason (R): Article 326 provides that elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies shall be on the basis of universal adult suffrage.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains how political equality is secured through adult franchise.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity form a union of trinity.
Reason (R): Divorcing one from the other defeats the very purpose of democracy.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: This is Dr. Ambedkar's statement. Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of why they form a trinity.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Social justice means equal treatment of all citizens without any social distinction.
Reason (R): The Preamble is justiciable and enforceable in courts of law.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is true. Reason is false because the Preamble is non-justiciable.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble secures economic justice directly.
Reason (R): Economic justice is inspired by the French Revolution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false. The Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot secure justice directly (it is done through DPSP/FRs). Reason is false (inspired by Russian Revolution).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Liberty of belief and worship is protected as a Fundamental Right.
Reason (R): Articles 25-28 of the Constitution provide for the Right to Freedom of Religion.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why/how the liberty is protected as a Fundamental Right.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Single citizenship is a measure to promote fraternity in India.
Reason (R): Double citizenship would lead to regional divisions and weaken national unity.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains how single citizenship helps in building fraternity and national unity.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble promises equality of wealth to all citizens.
Reason (R): Economic justice aims to remove inequalities in income and status.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false. The Preamble does not promise equality of wealth (it promises equality of status and opportunity). Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble guarantees the dignity of the individual.
Reason (R): The value of dignity is reinforced by Part III Fundamental Rights (like Article 21).
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of how individual dignity is legally secured.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble were adopted from the French Revolution.
Statement II: The ideals of Social, Economic, and Political Justice were adopted from the American Revolution.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because justice ideals are from the Russian Revolution.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble guarantees Equality of status and opportunity.
Statement II: Civic equality is secured under Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship is absolute under the Indian Constitution.
Statement II: Fundamental Rights are justiciable, while DPSP are non-justiciable.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect (liberties are qualified). Statement II is correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Fraternity in the Preamble assures the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.
Statement II: The word 'Integrity' was in the original Preamble in 1950.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Integrity was added in 1976.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Political equality is established through Article 325 and Article 326.
Statement II: Economic equality is promoted under Article 39 of the DPSP.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q: Why is liberty without equality dangerous in a democratic society?
masteryZone.sol: Because without equality, liberty would produce the dominance of the few over the many, destroying the democratic foundation of the society.

masteryZone.q: Why is fraternity essential for the success of liberty and equality?
masteryZone.sol: Because without fraternity, liberty and equality cannot become a natural course of social interactions; it is fraternity that binds the individuals as a nation.

masteryZone.q: Why did the 42nd Amendment add the word 'Integrity'?
masteryZone.sol: To reinforce territorial unity and counter secessionist movements that threatened the integrity of the Indian nation.

masteryZone.q: How does Article 17 of the Constitution secure civic equality?
masteryZone.sol: By abolishing untouchability and forbidding its practice in any form, thereby removing a major social barrier to equality of status.

masteryZone.q: How does the Constitution secure political equality to all citizens?
masteryZone.sol: Through two provisions: 1) Article 325 (no discrimination in electoral rolls). 2) Article 326 (universal adult franchise, ensuring every citizen's vote has equal value).

masteryZone.q: How does Article 39 of the DPSP support the Preamble's objective of economic justice?
masteryZone.sol: It directs the state to secure: 1) Equal right to adequate livelihood. 2) Equal pay for equal work. 3) Prevention of concentration of wealth.

masteryZone.q: A state policy provides special reservations in public employment for women. A challenge is filed stating this violates 'equality of opportunity'. Analyze this in light of the Preamble and Article 16.
masteryZone.sol: The challenge is invalid. The Preamble promises equality of status and opportunity. Under Article 16(4) and Article 15(3), the state is empowered to make special provisions for women and backward classes to ensure substantive equality, making reservation valid.

masteryZone.q: A regional political party demands state-wise citizenship to protect local interests. Analyze the impact of this demand on the Preamble's objective of Fraternity.
masteryZone.sol: The demand violates Fraternity. The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship to foster a common national brotherhood. Double citizenship (state-wise) would promote regionalism, create divisions, and weaken national integration.

masteryZone.q: The government nationalizes all private educational institutions to ensure equal access. A group of minorities challenges this scheme. Evaluate the balance of values here.
masteryZone.sol: This involves a conflict between: 1) The state's goal of social justice and equality of opportunity. 2) The minority rights to establish and administer institutions under Article 30. The Supreme Court has ruled that while state regulations for quality are valid, absolute nationalization of minority institutions violates Article 30.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of Liberty and how it is protected under the Indian Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Liberty means the absence of restraints on individual activities, while simultaneously providing opportunities for the development of individual personalities. It is protected under Part III Fundamental Rights (Articles 19, 25-28). It is not absolute but subject to reasonable restrictions (public order, security, etc.).

masteryZone.q: Explain the three dimensions of Equality guaranteed by the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: The three dimensions are: 1) Civic Equality: Secured through Articles 14 (equality before law) to 18 (abolition of titles). 2) Political Equality: Secured through Article 325 (non-discriminatory electoral rolls) and Article 326 (adult suffrage). 3) Economic Equality: Promoted through DPSP (Article 39, ensuring adequate livelihood and equal pay).

masteryZone.q: Explain the meaning and significance of 'Dignity of the Individual' as part of Fraternity.
masteryZone.sol: Dignity of the individual means that the Constitution guarantees that the personality of each individual is sacred. It is secured through Fundamental Rights (like Article 21, right to live with dignity) and Directive Principles, ensuring that every citizen has a decent standard of life.

sections.title: 3. Judicial Status and Amendability of the Preamble

masteryZone.q: In which case did the Supreme Court first rule that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
opts: Berubari Union case (1960)
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)
LIC of India case (1995)
Golaknath case (1967)
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court first recognized the Preamble as a part of the Constitution in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), reversing its 1960 stand.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is amendable under Article 368. However, which of the following limits this power?
opts: Presidential approval
Basic Structure Doctrine
State Legislature consent
Judicial veto
masteryZone.sol: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the court ruled that while the Preamble is amendable, the elements that form the 'Basic Structure' cannot be destroyed.

masteryZone.q: In the Berubari Union Case (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is:
opts: A part of the Constitution
Not a part of the Constitution
An integral part of the Constitution
A source of legislative power
masteryZone.sol: In the Berubari Case (1960), the Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following cases reaffirmed the Preamble's status as an 'integral part' of the Constitution in 1995?
opts: LIC of India case
S.R. Bommai case
Minerva Mills case
Golaknath case
masteryZone.sol: The LIC of India case (1995) reaffirmed the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following is a key feature of the Preamble regarding its enforceability?
opts: It is justiciable in High Courts only
It is non-justiciable
It can override Fundamental Rights
It is enforceable by the President
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble is non-justiciable. Its provisions are not enforceable in any court of law.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following cases are associated with the discussion on the legal status of the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: Berubari Union Case (1960)
Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
LIC of India Case (1995)
Vishaka Case (1997)
masteryZone.sol: Berubari, Kesavananda, and LIC cases are key cases defining the Preamble's status. Vishaka case is related to sexual harassment guidelines.

masteryZone.q: What are the rules regarding the legal nature of the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: It is non-justiciable
It is neither a source of power nor a limitation on legislative powers
It can be used to interpret ambiguous constitutional provisions
It can be used to strike down any law directly
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble is non-justiciable, neither grants nor restricts power, and helps interpret ambiguous text. It cannot be used to strike down a law directly.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are part of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution as reflected in the Preamble? (Select all that apply)
opts: Sovereignty of India
Secular character
Republican form of government
Absolute supremacy of the Executive
masteryZone.sol: Sovereignty, secularism, democracy, and republic are part of the Basic Structure. Absolute executive supremacy is not.

masteryZone.q: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, what arguments led the court to hold the Preamble as a part of the Constitution? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was introduced, debated, and voted upon in the Constituent Assembly
It has the same enacting history as other provisions
It is placed at the end of the Constitution
It is justiciable
masteryZone.sol: The court relied on the fact that the Preamble went through the exact same enactment process (debated/voted) in the Constituent Assembly. Placement at the end or justiciability were not the reasons.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are correct about Preamble amendments? (Select all that apply)
opts: Can be amended under Article 368
Basic features of Preamble cannot be amended
Has been amended only once
Requires a special referendum of the public to amend
masteryZone.sol: It is amendable under Article 368, subject to Basic Structure, and has been amended only once. No referendum is required in India.

masteryZone.q: The Supreme Court in the Berubari Union Case (1960) ruled that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: False. It ruled that the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: The Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973 established the Basic Structure Doctrine, which limits the amendability of the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Basic Structure doctrine prevents the Parliament from amending the core values in the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is enforceable in the Supreme Court under Article 32.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced under Article 32.

masteryZone.q: In the LIC of India Case (1995), the Supreme Court reversed its Kesavananda stand and held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: False. It reaffirmed that it is an integral part of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Where the language of a constitutional article is clear and unambiguous, the Preamble can be used to override it.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Preamble is only used as an aid to interpretation when the language of an article is ambiguous.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble was enacted by the Constituent Assembly after all other provisions of the Constitution had been passed.
masteryZone.sol: True. This was done to ensure the Preamble matched the enacted provisions.

masteryZone.q: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended the Preamble to add the word 'Democratic'.
masteryZone.sol: False. It added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'. 'Democratic' was already there.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is neither a source of legislative power nor a prohibition on legislative power.
masteryZone.sol: True. This is a key legal rule regarding the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble was declared NOT a part of the Constitution in the ______ Union Case (1960).
masteryZone.sol: The Berubari Union Case (1960).

masteryZone.q: The Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution in the ______ Bharati Case (1973).
masteryZone.sol: The Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973).

masteryZone.q: The Preamble was held to be an 'integral part' of the Constitution in the ______ of India Case (1995).
masteryZone.sol: The LIC of India Case (1995).

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is ______-justiciable, meaning its provisions are not enforceable in court.
masteryZone.sol: It is non-justiciable.

masteryZone.q: Amendments to the Preamble under Article 368 cannot violate the ______ Structure of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: They cannot violate the Basic Structure.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble has been amended exactly ______ time(s) so far.
masteryZone.sol: It has been amended only once.

masteryZone.q: The 42nd Amendment Act of ______ added three words to the Preamble.
masteryZone.sol: It was passed in 1976.

masteryZone.q: In case of ambiguity in constitutional provisions, the Preamble acts as an aid to ______.
masteryZone.sol: It is used as an aid to interpretation.

masteryZone.q: Match the cases with their corresponding rulings on the Preamble:

options.text: Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution
Preamble IS a part of the Constitution
Preamble is an INTEGRAL part of the Constitution

masteryZone.sol: Berubari: Not a part; Kesavananda: Part; LIC: Integral part.

masteryZone.q: Match the constitutional terms with their status/attributes:
masteryZone.sol: Art. 368: Amendment; Basic Structure: Limit on amendments; Justiciability: Non-enforceable nature.

masteryZone.q: Match the amendments/cases with their outcomes:

options.text: Called Preamble a key to open the mind of makers

masteryZone.sol: 42nd: Added three words; Kesavananda: Amendable; Berubari: Key to open mind of makers.

masteryZone.q: In which case did the Supreme Court first declare the Preamble as part of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

masteryZone.q: What is the key limitation on amending the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: The Basic Structure of the Constitution cannot be altered or destroyed.

masteryZone.q: Can a citizen sue the government for violating Preamble values?
masteryZone.sol: No, because the Preamble is non-justiciable.

masteryZone.q: Who did the Berubari case say the Preamble is a key to open the mind of?
masteryZone.sol: The constitution makers (framers).

masteryZone.q: What amendment added the word 'Secular' to the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: Is the Preamble a source of power to the Parliament?
masteryZone.sol: No, it is neither a source of power nor a limitation on power.

masteryZone.q: Which 1995 case reaffirmed the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: LIC of India case (1995).

masteryZone.q: Why was the Preamble enacted after the other parts of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure that it was in conformity with all other provisions of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble can be amended under Article 368.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation because being a part of the Constitution makes it amendable under Art. 368.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is non-justiciable.
Reason (R): Courts can use the Preamble to interpret ambiguous provisions of the Constitution.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. However, R is not the correct explanation of why it is non-justiciable.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The 42nd Amendment added the word 'Democratic' to the Preamble.
Reason (R): The Preamble has been amended only once.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false (Democratic was in original). Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble cannot restrict the powers of the legislature.
Reason (R): The Preamble is not a limitation or prohibition upon the powers of the legislature.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Berubari Case (1960) ruled that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court reversed this ruling in the Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973).
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is false. Reason is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The LIC of India Case (1995) confirmed this status.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why/how it is recognized as an integral part.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Any amendment to the Preamble can be challenged in court.
Reason (R): Amendments to the Preamble are subject to the Basic Structure Doctrine.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why amendments can be challenged (if they violate basic structure).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble serves as a prefix to the Constitution.
Reason (R): The Preamble was drafted by K.M. Munshi.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Assertion is true. Reason is false because it was based on Nehru's Objective Resolution, not drafted by Munshi.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble can be used to override clear provisions of the Constitution.
Statement II: The Preamble is an aid to interpret ambiguous constitutional provisions.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect. Statement II is correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble was declared a part of the Constitution in the Berubari Union Case.
Statement II: The Kesavananda Bharati case overruled the Berubari Union case regarding the Preamble's status.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect. Statement II is correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble is non-justiciable.
Statement II: Non-justiciability means it cannot be used by the judiciary for any purpose.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because courts can still use it for interpretation.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble was amended in 1976 to add 'Socialist' and 'Secular'.
Statement II: The 42nd Amendment did not add the word 'Integrity'.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Integrity was also added.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The Preamble can be amended under Article 368.
Statement II: The amendability of the Preamble is subject to the Basic Structure Doctrine.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Supreme Court change its stance in the Kesavananda Bharati case from the Berubari case?
masteryZone.sol: Because it realized that the Preamble went through the exact same enactment process (debated, voted, and passed) in the Constituent Assembly as the other parts of the Constitution, making it an organic part of the document.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Preamble considered non-justiciable?
masteryZone.sol: To prevent citizens from suing the government directly to implement abstract ideals (like fraternity or absolute justice) without specific enabling laws passed by the legislature.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Preamble key to understand the minds of the constitution makers?
masteryZone.sol: Because it outlines the core values, political philosophy, and basic objectives that the makers wanted the independent Indian nation to follow.

masteryZone.q: How does the Basic Structure Doctrine protect the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: It prohibits the Parliament from using its amendment power under Article 368 to delete or destroy key values in the Preamble (such as Secularism, Democracy, and Sovereignty) which are recognized as basic features.

masteryZone.q: How can the Preamble assist the judiciary when an article of the Constitution is ambiguous?
masteryZone.sol: The judges can refer to the Preamble's goals to clarify the intent of the framers and choose the legal interpretation that best promotes those goals.

masteryZone.q: How does the LIC of India case (1995) support the status of the Preamble?
masteryZone.sol: It strongly reaffirmed the Kesavananda ruling, stating that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution, settling any lingering doubts.

masteryZone.q: A new constitutional amendment seeks to replace the words 'Democratic Republic' with 'Democratic Monarchy'. Analyze the validity of this amendment using Preamble status.
masteryZone.sol: The amendment is invalid. Under the Kesavananda Bharati ruling, the Preamble's republican character is part of the Basic Structure. Replacing it with a monarchy destroys the basic structure, which is forbidden under Article 368 limits.

masteryZone.q: A petitioner files a public interest litigation (PIL) to force the government to immediately provide equal status to all regional languages based on the Preamble's promise of Equality. Analyze the court's response.
masteryZone.sol: The court will reject the petition. The Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced directly to create new rights or force government action in the absence of specific constitutional articles or parliamentary legislation.

masteryZone.q: A law is passed that restricts the entry of certain foreign organizations. The organizations challenge this using the Preamble's value of 'Liberty'. Evaluate this challenge.
masteryZone.sol: The challenge will fail. 1) The Preamble is non-justiciable. 2) Liberty under the Constitution is qualified and subject to national sovereignty and security. The state has the sovereign power to regulate foreign entry, which overrides abstract claims of liberty.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of the Berubari Union Case (1960) and its limitations.
masteryZone.sol: In the Berubari Case, the SC held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution, although it is a key to open the mind of the makers. Its limitation was that it failed to recognize that the Preamble was voted and passed in the Constituent Assembly just like any other article, which was later corrected in 1973.

masteryZone.q: Explain the amendability of the Preamble and the only amendment made to it.
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble can be amended under Article 368, but its basic features cannot be altered. It has been amended only once by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, which added the words: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.

masteryZone.q: Explain the difference between justiciable and non-justiciable parts of the Constitution, using the Preamble as an example.
masteryZone.sol: Justiciable parts (like Fundamental Rights) can be directly enforced in courts, and citizens can sue for their violation. Non-justiciable parts (like the Preamble and DPSPs) contain goals and guidelines but cannot be directly enforced by courts to compel state action without specific laws.
